findings.finding: Trailers are taken from any line of the commit body whose trimmed text starts with 'Tier1-Allow:', not from the trailer block. An indented example in a commit message (such as the CONTRIBUTING example) becomes a real suppression. A wrapped prose line that happens to start with 'Tier1-Allow:' becomes a LINT-05 MUST failure (diff.go:206).
findings.suggestion: Read only real trailers: git log --format='%H%x00%(trailers:key=Tier1-Allow,valueonly,unfold)%x1e', or git interpret-trailers --parse. Add a test with an indented example in a body paragraph.

findings.finding: Suppress records each trailer once (rule, glob, reason, commit) and drops the findings it cleared. A broad glob such as 'RELAY-07 relay/**' therefore hides what it suppressed from the human at sign-off, which works against Decision 5's 'cannot silence a check without the human seeing that it did'. counts.suppressed counts trailers, not findings. Unused trailers are not listed at all.
findings.suggestion: Carry the cleared findings (rule, file, line, message) under each suppression entry in the report and in report.schema.json, print them in the suppressed section, and count findings. Optionally list trailers that matched nothing as hints.

findings.finding: The changed-line ranges come from the committed diff (base..HEAD), but the analyzers (packages.Load) and golangci-lint (golangci.go:190) read the working tree. With uncommitted edits, which is normal during make lint, positions do not match the ranges. A committed violation shifted by a local edit is dropped, and an uncommitted one can land on a 'changed' line. CONTRIBUTING says 'committed changes only'. CI checkouts are clean, so only local runs and agent sessions are affected.
findings.suggestion: Warn when tracked .go files differ from HEAD (git status --porcelain), or exit 2 under a strict flag. Alternatively, run those two stages in a temporary worktree at HEAD.

findings.finding: The task-11 retune drops every comment when it compares tokens. That also drops directives: //go:build constraints, //go:embed, //export and the cgo preamble. A change that only edits '//go:build linux' to '//go:build linux || darwin' in driver/*.go changes which platforms compile the file, but it is treated as comment-only. drivers-claim, bootstrap-surface and seam-contract then never see it.
findings.suggestion: Scan with scanner.ScanComments, and keep comments that start with '//go:', '// +build' or '//export' (and the comment group just before import "C") as tokens. Add a test case for a build-constraint-only change.

findings.finding: An explicit -design PATH that does not exist at HEAD, or does not parse, is kept with Design.Err set, and Err is never reported. Examples are a typo or a Windows path such as docs\design\x.md. Because NoDesignInDiff (line 110) tests len(List) > 0, such a path silently satisfies FLOW-01 while it adds nothing to the drivers/seams/rules claim.
findings.suggestion: Normalize explicit paths with filepath.ToSlash. Fail with exit 2 when an explicit design is missing or unparsable, and name the bad path.

findings.finding: Three golangci-lint versions are in play. The tier1 CI and release jobs pin v2.5.0 (main.yml:37, release.yml:66, and golangci.go:154's install hint). The lint job installs @latest (main.yml:20). Local sessions run 2.6.2. revive and errorlint output can differ between versions, so the same diff can pass locally and fail in CI or at release, against LINT-05's 'reproducible'.
findings.suggestion: Pin one version, for example in a Makefile or env variable that both workflows and golangci.Install read, and match it to the toolchain sessions use.
